title: A pointwise 2-converse for elliptic curves with rational two-torsion
main_claim: Theorem 1.1: Let E/Q have E(Q)[2] ≠ 0 and 2^∞-Selmer corank s_2(E) equal to 0 or 1. Then ord_{s=1} L(E,s) = rank E(Q) = s_2(E), and Sha(E/Q) is finite. No condition is placed on the reduction at 2.

issues.location: sections/cyclotomic.tex, Lemma cy:residual and the uniform integrality (cy:uniform-integrality); sections/ring-limits.tex and ring-determinants.tex (inner/outer limit constructions)
issues.description: This is a coverage limitation, not a demonstrated error. The proof relies on several very long constructions that I could not fully verify at this depth: residual concentration of the positive Iwasawa complex over O[G] (based on Ferrero-Washington and Kummer-theory dimension counts), the use of Kato Thm 12.5(3) as a rational divisibility at p=2, the two-stage limits of the ring-class Selmer complexes, and the proof of the graph address lemma. Each one carries a constant that must stay uniform as b and #Q grow. The paper says it is uniform each time, but I could only follow the argument at outline level.
issues.evidence: 'with C_int independent of S, h_0, G, and b'; 'Lemma rl:residual-bound bounds the minimal models in terms of E,A and the number of retained derivative primes, not the active conductor support.'

coverage: I read all of introduction, preliminaries, nonvanishing and pointwise (the assembly: interfaces, seeds/reserves/packets, even estimate, rough companion, height comparison, odd lower bound, split witness, odd base). I read most of cyclotomic (both theorems, the Fourier intersection, the binary congruence lemma, the residual lemma, Kato coefficient map, Euler corrections, the central determinant formula, the missing-vertex proof). In coefficients I read the even system, Kummer detection, theta bridge, odd detection, minimum, operators, traces, inertia and symbol interface. In graphs I read realization, the address statement and forests. In ring-determinants I read only the closing part (unused-prime removal, Schur/Laurent elimination, clearing, the bits lemma, the transfer lemma, the proof of rd:missing-vertex). I did not read ring-limits beyond its statements, the early ring-determinants sections (local model, derivative switch, central formula), or the proofs of the network and program lemmas in graphs. I checked these by hand: the degree bound and parity in the Chevalley-Warning step of Lemma cy:binary; the identity O ∩ Λ[1/2] = Λ; the BSD consistency of D(h) = v(L_*) - 2w - s, including Tamagawa 2^{t_q} at I0* twists; the Gross-Zagier normalization in the height ratio (|h|√|k| against √|hh_*|); the inequality chain in Prop pw:odd-lower; the recurrence congruences in co:operators and pw:recurrence (Δ_1-Δ_0 mod 4, b_s ≡ p^s); the identity (a-1)(a-p-1)/4 giving a_p ≡ p+1 mod 8 and the inert-prime witness (a-1-p)/4 odd; the good-simple ≡ 2 mod 4 argument; the root-number sign in pw:rough-companion; and the congruence and valuation bookkeeping in Lemma rd:binary-transfer (M-2c). Every check came out consistent.
